final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful, but it does not satisfy the missing policy condition. Under the policy text, rollout controls, rollback capability, monitoring, and a 5% launch do not by themselves cure the disclosed weakness when the affected segment remains exposed. The Actor now concedes that point and also concedes there is no evidence that disclosure has already been completed. That means the narrower position is only a potentially compliant path if disclosure is actually made and the certification is explicitly conditional on it. Because this condition remains unproven in the admissible record, the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. The record therefore supports rejecting the broader certification rationale as not evidentially established, while recognizing that a compliant-with-caveats outcome could become supportable if the missing disclosure evidence were produced.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed or locked for launch.
The affected Spanish-language billing support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout while still below target.
There is still no reviewed and approved risk acceptance addressing continued exposure of that segment.
The narrowed conditional-certification theory depends on an unresolved compliance predicate: actual disclosure or other policy-satisfying coverage.
The recommended certification action remains broader than what the admissible record currently proves.
